title: Commonweal: Music for the Common Good
made_with: Vigil Box (BeepBox 4.2.2 synth) by VigilTech; composed in tools/studio/music.js
mastering: RMS matched to -16 dBFS, soft knee limiting under -1 dBFS

tracks.title: Keystone
tracks.subtitle: Theme of Commonweal
tracks.about: The main theme. A bell melody rises stone by stone over a minor progression and builds to a full band, the way an arch stands once its keystone is set.

tracks.title: Open Standard
tracks.subtitle: Every part compatible
tracks.about: One shared format carried to every corner of the nation, so every machine can talk to every other: fast, rhythmic, always transmitting.

tracks.title: Early Warning
tracks.subtitle: Signals in the numbers
tracks.about: A steady pulse that keeps measuring and answering: problems caught early, by the people closest to them.

tracks.title: Algedonic Signal
tracks.subtitle: The alarm that skips the queue
tracks.about: Beer's pain-and-pleasure alarm: a signal of harm that goes straight to whoever can act. It starts as a warning and ends resolved.

tracks.title: Supply Lines
tracks.subtitle: The trucks keep rolling
tracks.about: When supply is threatened, coordination keeps food and fuel moving to every town. Bright and driving: the nation looking after its own.

tracks.title: Hearth
tracks.subtitle: A waltz for home and tradition
tracks.about: A gentle waltz on plucked strings and organ, for family, faith and the customs handed down.

tracks.title: Viable System
tracks.subtitle: Systems within systems
tracks.about: Stafford Beer's model of a system that governs itself, where every part is a whole and every whole a part. The melody answers itself in canon.

tracks.title: Commonweal
tracks.subtitle: Finale
tracks.about: The Keystone theme returns in a major key: the common good, held in common.
